newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury official outlines credit union study.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury official outlines credit union study.

text.p: A Treasury Department study due next September will review regulations dealing with corporate credit unions, the National Credit Union Share Insurance Fund, and the safety and soundness of credit unions, a Treasury official said Friday.

In recently enacted legislation, Congress required Treasury to conduct the study, Richard Carnell, assistant Treasury secretary, said in a speech prepared for the California Credit Union League convention.
A copy of the speech was released in Washington.
The study will also cover the National Credit Union Share Insurance Fund, including whether it should be administered by a group other than the National Credit Union Administration, he said.
Congress also required the study to evaluate the 10 largest corporate credit unions, Carnell said.
"I can't tell you today what conclusions we'll draw in our forthcoming study. I can tell you that we'll approach it objectively," Carnell said.
